business_rules.statement: The rendered capability list and the runtime authorisation decision are generated from one configuration source, so a divergence is a build defect rather than a behavioural drift.
Forward parity: every rendered control for every identity shape corresponds to a permitted action. Failing count must be zero.
Reverse parity: every permitted action corresponds to a rendered control or to a capability explicitly recorded as headless. Failing count must be zero.
Offline parity: every Frontline action's behaviour offline matches its declared status, and no surface displays a command state beyond queued or available for delivery for an offline device.
Floor parity: no identity shape, tenant configuration, suspension state, or caller class permits an action that would breach a platform floor or one of the six enforced invariants.
A handoff is a record, not a notification. A handoff whose only evidence is that an email was sent has not occurred.
The four state families — notification, command, capture, handoff — are distinct and are never collapsed. No surface may show a handoff as complete because a notification was sent.
Acknowledge is not resolve. Acknowledge means 'I have seen this and own it'; resolve means 'it is dealt with'; both are explicit, timestamped actions on the Delivery Operations Hub-owned record.
Where a handoff routes to a role, all on-shift holders at the Location are notified and the first acknowledgement claims the item, removing it from other actionable queues while leaving it visible.
Routing targets roles, never individuals. Person resolution happens at runtime in the Delivery Operations Hub against the roster of role-holders currently on shift.
A notification must never be the only mechanism enforcing a hold, a qualification, an authorisation, an approval, a suspension, or a device command.
business_rules.enforcement_point: on-device deterministic layer plus command channel

business_rules.statement: No handoff may bypass role-based access control, cross a tenant boundary, bypass qualification, specification, evaluation, approval, publication, or the Severity 1 hold and release rules.
The handoff record and its audit event commit in one transaction; an action that cannot be audited does not happen.
Notifications are queued and sent on the platform's two channels, in-app and email, and only those. In-app notifications cannot be muted.
Every handoff in sections 18.4 to 18.9 is defined against all nineteen attributes. No attribute may be omitted; where it does not apply the entry reads 'Not applicable — [specific reason]'.
Evidence is immutable at creation and corrections are append-only annotations.
Platform and tenant roles are separate security domains. A Tenant Admin has no platform authority; there is no Tenant Super Admin; there is no Quality Director role.

Record-level operational content is reached only through one of three named access classes: the normal support session, the compliance-emergency path, and the JBS access grant. No ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console.
A tenant must hold an approver role whenever a Job exists; the platform refuses any action that would leave zero approver-capable holders or zero Tenant Admins.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Delivery Operations Hub role assignment service

business_rules.statement: Approval requests are first-class records carrying proposer, change class, object reference, diff, rationale, state in the set pending/approved/returned/applied, approver, timestamps and audit reference; nothing applies silently.

No agent, capability, or composed behaviour goes live without passing its evaluation scenarios — a hard gate binding every operator of the console including the root. Approval does not substitute for the gate.

A support session is read-only without exception; no write capability exists inside it, and a data repair is not support — anything that changes tenant data goes through the compliance-emergency path.
Banner text is fixed in the source: 'Platform support is viewing your workspace. Started [time]. Engineer [name]. End session.'

Exactly five tenant roles are fixed at V1; custom roles are deferred beyond V1; scopes are Tenant, Site and Area, held simultaneously; multi-role is additive; the audit log records identity and action, not 'acting as role'.
Editing a shift never retroactively re-stamps completed runs.

A role change reaches a device-bound user through the command channel and applies at the device's next sync; the Delivery Operations Hub must not display the change as in force on that device until the device confirms.
Classification happens on-device at the instant of capture, including offline, and a Severity 1 hold is placed locally and immediately; only the delivery of escalation waits for connectivity.
A gate block encountered offline parks the run, the worker continues other assigned runs, and the parked run resumes when the clearance arrives.

A required supervisor sign-off forces a sync before sign-off as a designated high-risk action and captures the supervisor's identity against that authorisation only, without ending the worker's session.

Mid-run substitution is supervisor-initiated with a reason; the substitute receives a structured handover of last completed step, open flags and current state; pre-substitution steps remain attributed to the original worker.
In-flight runs are never re-based onto a newer workflow version; the run stays pinned to the version it started on.

The Severity 1 floor never moves: automatic lot freeze plus Quality-Manager-only release plus escalation, platform-fixed; tenants may add actions to any level and may never remove the Severity 1 floor.
The freeze lands on the Lot where a lot exists, the Unit where work is serialized, and otherwise the Run, whose output is quarantined and whose run is blocked pending Quality Manager disposition.

Gate items follow a 10-minute window at Severity 1 and 30 minutes otherwise, configurable per severity level; a waiting item re-routes if nobody responds in time; it never executes on its own and never silently expires.

Lane B proposals are decided by the Quality Manager and above, with Supervisors observing and annotating; undecided proposals age with a 30-day stale flag copied to the Quality Manager's digest and never expire.
No route, role, configuration, tier, work type, risk class, or tag permits any identity other than a Quality Manager to release a lot hold.
No timer, agent action, escalation tier, record-finish transition, or tenant configuration releases a hold.
The hold panel displays per-device confirmation state and never shows `in force` until every relevant device has confirmed.
Nothing is purged; the tenant-set retention value is a hot-retrievability horizon, default 15 years, and beyond it data tiers to lower-cost storage and remains retrievable.

Worker personal data anonymises at 24 months for standard commercial tenants — measurement, result and evidence survive and identity becomes an opaque worker identifier — and never in Regulated-Industry mode; anonymisation is the platform's one irreversible act.

Authoring never rides the learning pipeline: structural insight travels to authors as a watch item or authoring recommendation and takes effect only through normal Studio authoring and versioned publication.
Every activity row carries exactly one Accountable role; accountability appears exactly once per row, because two accountable roles is the same as none.

The absolute rule: no timer, escalation tier, fallback delivery, agent, scheduled job, tenant configuration, tier entitlement, platform setting, or account — including the root — may cause an approval, release, adoption, publication, clearance, or any other authorising decision without a recorded human decision. Absence of a decision is never a decision.
The permitted chain where no authorised substitute exists is fixed and ordered: escalation, then controlled hold, then safe stop. There is no fourth step and no bypass.

Three structural prohibitions in the handoff state machine: no transition from Created or Delivered directly to Resolved; no transition out of Cancelled, Expired or Resolved other than to Reconciled; no automatic transition into Actioned or Resolved from any timer, agent or tier.
Out-of-order authorisation events never resolve by last-write-wins; the safety-favouring restrictive state applies pending human (Quality Manager) resolution.
A late-arriving Severity 1 capture places a fresh hold even where the lot was previously released.
No operational data originates in the Delivery Operations Hub itself; every capture arrives from the Frontline Worker Application.
Tenants may make the platform stricter than default; they may never make it looser than the platform floor, and the platform rejects a looser-than-floor value rather than logging it.
Every consequential write in the Hub commits with its audit entry in the same database transaction; a forced audit-write failure rolls back the business write.
There are exactly five command classes on the platform: lot release, reassignment or substitution, qualification clearance, suspension, and version change. No sixth class exists at V1.
A newer command of the same class against the same target supersedes an undelivered older one, and the older one is never delivered.
The Hub offers no control that pauses, stops or force-syncs a run or a device; pausing or stopping a run is deliberately impossible from the Client Command Center for every role.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Hub and Command Center control surfaces

business_rules.statement: When the browser session cannot reach the platform, every write control is disabled rather than queued, and no local draft of a governance act is retained in the browser.
Both Band A and Band B are V1: the scope is signed as A plus B together; the split is an internal build-sequencing lens only and carries no commercial or acceptance meaning.

decisions.question: What is the retry budget for handoff creation and for notification delivery?
options: a time box scaled by severity
decisions.impact: Too small refuses handoffs on transient contention; too large delays a Severity 1 escalation

decisions.question: What is the nobody-on-shift escalation default? Carried as the source's own open drafting value.
options: fallback to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery
decisions.status: open — source's own open drafting value, preserved
decisions.impact: Anchors every fallback in Chapter 18

decisions.question: Should Studio submissions, pending_approval Jobs, returned platform proposals, and undecided version adoptions carry aging behaviour?
decisions.impact: Without visible aging they become invisible stalls; expiry would violate stated preference

decisions.question: Is a support session opened self-service by Support against a valid ticket, or granted per session or per tenant by an Admin?
decisions.impact: Changes the Admin's workload and the tenant's assurance story

decisions.question: May a JBS access grant carry write capability into tenant data?
options: write only when the grant is also an emergency-class session
decisions.impact: Affects the claim that the compliance-emergency path is the only class with write

decisions.question: Is a root-unavailability continuity procedure required for critical-class decisions?
options: a second break-glass root credential held in escrow
decisions.impact: Compliance suspension and emergency pause are critical class and time-sensitive

decisions.question: What happens when the nobody-on-shift fallback target — the Quality Manager role — has no holder at all?
options: Route to the Tenant Admin as an alarm only
block tenant configuration that permits the state
require a minimum Quality Manager count per tenant
decisions.status: Client Decision Required — newly raised in this chapter
decisions.impact: The never-resolves-to-nobody guarantee has a hole where a Severity 1 hold needs a decider

decisions.question: Does a role hierarchy exist for substitute sign-off, and if so what is it?
options: restrict substitution to the Quality Manager as the single higher authority
decisions.impact: §7.13.3 hierarchy contradicts §3.5/§4.8.4 additive non-hierarchical roles

decisions.question: What happens to a claimed but unresolved item when the claimant goes off shift?
options: claim auto-releases at shift end and the item re-routes marked as a re-route
claim persists but the item additionally re-notifies the role
decisions.impact: A surviving claim can park a Severity 1 request with someone who has gone home

decisions.question: How do in-flight handoffs behave in a compliance-suspended tenant?
options: Freeze handoffs in place and resume on exit
cancel and reconcile all open handoffs at suspension
permit disposition only through the compliance-emergency path
decisions.impact: Compliance suspension blocks all logins, so no tenant identity can acknowledge or resolve

decisions.question: Is the Site level a required minimum in the location hierarchy?
decisions.adopted_working_position: the level is mandatory and the default Site is auto-created, so the requirement never blocks onboarding
decisions.status: Derived Clarification — adopted working position, adopted 2026-08-14, client ratification outstanding
decisions.impact: Determines whether onboarding can proceed without an explicit Site

decisions.question: On reconnection, does a device upload pending captures before or after pulling pending commands?
decisions.adopted_working_position: three phases — stop-class commands pulled and applied first, then every pending capture uploaded with nothing discarded, then enabling-class commands applied
decisions.status: Derived Clarification — adopted working position, adopted 2026-08-14, client ratification outstanding
decisions.impact: Determines whether a suspension, wipe or hold lands before more work is done

decisions.question: What is the Job-to-parent-node cardinality: one parent node per Job or one Area per Job as a hard constraint?
options: one parent node per Job at the configured depth
one Area per Job is a hard constraint
decisions.adopted_working_position: a Job anchors at the deepest parent node its tenant configured, Part II governing, so §4.5.1's 'one Area per Job is a hard constraint' wording is superseded by 'one parent node per Job'
decisions.status: Derived Clarification — adopted working position, adopted 2026-08-14, client ratification outstanding
decisions.impact: Determines Job binding depth and multi-area pairing behaviour

decisions.question: Does the Prevention Agent operate wholly under pre-authorised policy or route every action through a runtime human gate?
decisions.adopted_working_position: gating is declared per agent in the agent record's governance-binding field, binding the Prevention Agent to `authoring-time policy`, the Deviation and Containment Agent to `runtime human gate` for proposals beyond pre-authorised containment, and the Shift Handoff Agent to `none — reasoning agent`
decisions.status: Derived Clarification — adopted working position, adopted 2026-08-14, client ratification outstanding
decisions.impact: Determines whether agent actions need a per-event runtime gate

decisions.question: Does three-stage Author/Reviewer/Release sign-off govern, or does an approved Lane B proposal auto-publish a patch version with no second approval?
options: §5.11.1 explicit human sign-off at each of three stages
§5.16.3 and §6.7.4 auto-publish a patch version with no second approval, no ceremony
decisions.impact: Governs the Hub's version-binding behaviour and Studio bypass risk

decisions.question: Do Plant Manager and Quality Director exist as roles? §6.1.3 lists them while §3.5 fixes five roles and states there is no Quality Director.
options: Plant Manager / Quality Director as Command Center user group with escalation-fallback duties
decisions.impact: Affects the unacknowledged shift-handoff-brief flag recipient and matrix cells

decisions.question: What is the meaning of the 'Supervisor+' and 'QM+' forms across five additive, non-hierarchical roles?
decisions.status: open — every handoff names the concrete role rather than relying on the plus form
decisions.impact: Undefined ordering makes matrix cells unimplementable

decisions.question: How does a remote wipe reach an offline device, and how long may a command remain pending if the device never returns?
decisions.impact: A device that never returns holds unsynced captures indefinitely

decisions.question: Should a Studio submission stalled in review carry aging behaviour?
options: a stale flag mirroring the Lane B 30-day precedent
decisions.impact: A stalled submission blocks a floor improvement invisibly

decisions.question: What is the defined display duration of an unmutable in-app announcement banner?
options: a per-announcement duration set at composition
decisions.impact: An unmutable banner with no defined end trains users to ignore banners

decisions.question: What are the linked-run handover mechanics and the no-show behaviour of a linked run carrying a live physical process?
decisions.impact: Auto-cancel of a linked run carrying a ten-hour cure must be confirmed by the client

decisions.question: Is there a Recovery Time Objective for lot disposition?
decisions.impact: Held material is idle production; an unstated objective becomes an implied one

decisions.question: What is the Recovery Time Objective for consolidated audit completeness?
decisions.impact: A tenant under external audit needs a stated time to a complete log

decisions.question: What form should an escalation delivery objective take?
options: a percentage of escalations delivered within the acknowledgement timer
decisions.impact: A second time value would compete with existing timers

decisions.question: What is the final identity of the five standard report data sets?
decisions.impact: Reports depend on data-set definition

decisions.question: Which fields are package-borne versus server-only? The package-borne field assignment is not enumerated.
decisions.impact: Determines whether an approved Lane B value auto-publishes a patch or applies immediately

decisions.question: Where does authority for engineering capability enablement sit versus tenant feature-value authority?
decisions.impact: Platform maker-checker scope boundary

decisions.question: How does 24-month anonymisation operate under the no-purge model?
decisions.impact: Anonymisation is the platform's one irreversible act

decisions.question: Is the surface named Delivery Operations Hub (Statement of Work) or Digital Operations Hub (blueprint commission)?
decisions.adopted_working_position: This chapter uses Delivery Operations Hub as the authoritative name
decisions.impact: Naming divergence across the specification

decisions.question: What are the record-finish window bounds? The finish-window bounds carry an unresolved contradiction.
decisions.impact: Floor of 24 hours and ceiling of 7 days are tested but contradictory in source

decisions.question: How is soft suspension released?
decisions.adopted_working_position: soft suspension released by an explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console
decisions.status: Derived Clarification — adopted working position, adopted 2026-08-14, client ratification outstanding
decisions.impact: Determines tenant reactivation path

decisions.question: Open decision referenced in Chapter 19 surface-level traceability; not resolved here.
decisions.impact: Retrieval behaviour beyond the hot-retrievability horizon

decisions.question: Open decision referenced in Chapter 19 surface-level traceability; not resolved here.
decisions.impact: Deletion behaviour under the no-purge model

contradictions.description: §5.11.1 requires explicit human sign-off at Author, Reviewer and Release Authority; §5.16.3 and §6.7.4 have an approved Lane B proposal auto-publish a patch version with no second approval, no ceremony.
conflicting_values: three-stage explicit human sign-off at each stage
auto-publish a patch version with no second approval, no ceremony

contradictions.description: §6.1.3 lists 'Plant Manager / Quality Director' as a Command Center user group with escalation-fallback duties while §3.5 states there is no Quality Director and fixes five roles.
conflicting_values: Plant Manager / Quality Director exist as a user group
five fixed roles, no Quality Director

contradictions.description: The authority matrices use 'Supervisor+' and 'QM+' without defining an ordering across five additive, non-hierarchical roles.
conflicting_values: plus form implies an ordering
roles are additive and non-hierarchical

contradictions.description: §2.1 marks the Site level recommended and open at drafting while §4.3.1 states the Site level is mandatory.
conflicting_values: Site level recommended and open
Site level is mandatory

contradictions.description: The Job's parent-node binding is contradictory between 'one parent node per Job' at the configured depth and 'one Area per Job is a hard constraint'.
conflicting_values: one parent node per Job at the configured depth
one Area per Job is a hard constraint

contradictions.description: §7.13.3 states a higher authority may sign off in a supervisor's place with a role hierarchy resolved from the Hub, while §3.5 and §4.8.4 state the five roles are additive and non-hierarchical and audit records identity, not 'acting as role'.
conflicting_values: a role hierarchy defines who may substitute for whom
five additive, non-hierarchical roles; no acting-as-role

contradictions.description: Whether the Prevention Agent is gated or operates wholly under pre-authorised policy is contradictory in the source.
conflicting_values: authoring-time policy, no per-event runtime gate
runtime human gate for every action

contradictions.description: The Statement of Work names the surface 'Delivery Operations Hub' throughout while the blueprint commission refers to it as the 'Digital Operations Hub'.
conflicting_values: Delivery Operations Hub
Digital Operations Hub

contradictions.description: The source does not state whether session opening is self-service by Support against a valid ticket or requires an Admin grant per session or per tenant.
conflicting_values: self-service against a valid ticket
Admin grant per session or per tenant

contradictions.description: The compliance-emergency path is named the only class with write capability, yet the JBS grant is described as a third class 'under the same discipline' without stating whether that includes read-only.
conflicting_values: compliance-emergency path is the only write class
JBS grant under the same discipline may carry write

contradictions.description: The nobody-on-shift fallback resolves to the Quality Manager role, which may itself have no holder, so the 'never resolves to no one' guarantee has a hole.
conflicting_values: escalation never resolves to no one
fallback target role may be empty

contradictions.description: The finish-window bounds carry an unresolved contradiction; the Hub tests a 24-hour floor and a 7-day ceiling.
conflicting_values: 24-hour platform floor
7-day ceiling

contradictions.description: The Statement of Work does not fix whether a reconnecting device uploads pending captures before or after pulling pending commands; safety and data integrity argue opposite orders.
conflicting_values: commands first (safety)
captures first (data integrity)

controls.label: Approve
controls.effect: Applies the platform change and commits the audit event in the same transaction

controls.label: Return with reason
controls.effect: Returns the proposal to the Platform Engineer with a categorised reason

controls.label: Critical class — root approval required
allowed_roles: non-root viewers see this in place of the action bar
controls.effect: Replaces the action bar; no control that could be mistaken for approval

controls.label: End session
controls.effect: Terminates the platform access session; recorded as tenant-initiated in both audit streams

controls.label: Release lot hold
controls.effect: Releases the hold; rides the command channel to every affected device

controls.label: Request release with a note
controls.effect: Creates an item for the Quality Manager; changes no hold state

controls.label: Mark evidence reviewed
controls.effect: Records evidence review against the screen's specification and proof requirements

controls.label: Annotate (append-only)
controls.effect: Adds an annotation that never edits or alters the original

controls.label: Approve
controls.effect: Gate item's intervention executes on approval

controls.label: Adjust within bounds and approve
controls.effect: Adjusts the proposed intervention within bounds, then executes it

controls.label: Decline with reason
controls.effect: Declines the gate item with a mandatory categorised reason

controls.label: Acknowledge
controls.effect: Writes the acknowledgement timestamp; never blocks shift start

controls.label: Annotate
controls.effect: Annotates a brief item; feeds the output-feedback loop

controls.label: Return with comments
controls.effect: Returns the submission to the Author with mandatory comments

controls.label: Advance
controls.effect: Advances the submission to the Release Authority stage

controls.label: Preview every screen
controls.effect: Previews each screen, instruction text, limits, coaching and deviation rules

controls.label: Resolve-All (sync conflicts)
controls.effect: Resolves sync conflicts in bulk; Supervisors may view only

controls.label: Filters: Area, severity, type and state
controls.effect: Filters the alert and escalation feed

controls.label: CSV and JSON export
controls.effect: Exports filtered audit-log results

controls.label: Role selector (five roles, no creation affordance)
controls.effect: Assigns one of exactly five fixed roles; custom-role creation is absent, not disabled

controls.label: Scope selector (Tenant, Site, Area)
controls.effect: Assigns scope; Location, Job and worker scoping are absent

controls.label: Approver-capable holders counter

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The parity suite itself cannot complete a dimension
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry the failed dimension once with an extended timeout
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Report the dimension as unverified and block the release
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No release; last-known-good deployment continues
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Defects fixed, suite re-run to a complete run with zero counts in the two failing quadrants

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The handoff record cannot be written (audit event cannot commit)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry against the same transaction boundary with an idempotency key of object reference, trigger event identifier and target role
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The triggering action is refused and surfaced to the initiator as a refusal, never as a success
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The operational object stays in its pre-handoff state under its pre-handoff owner; deterministic on-device enforcement untouched
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Initiator retries once the audit path is healthy; a scheduled sweep lists trigger events with no corresponding handoff

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An incomplete handoff record — created without mandatory attributes such as evidence references or reason code
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Creation validated at the service boundary; an incomplete record is rejected before commit
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where an attribute is unavailable outside the initiator's control, the handoff is created with evidence marked pending and the panel displays 'Evidence pending upload'
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A handoff with pending evidence may be acknowledged and claimed but may not be resolved
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On evidence arrival the record updates in place and the recipient is re-notified once, de-duplicated

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A collaboration path cannot be established because the tenant's role population is incomplete
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The Hub blocks the action that would remove the last approver-capable holder and names the reason
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the population is already incomplete, the tenant enters a controlled configuration hold — no Job may transition draft to pending_approval
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Existing in-flight runs complete, capture, sync, compute summaries and close; Severity 1 floor and deterministic gates remain in force
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Tenant Admin assigns a Quality Manager or designated equivalent approver; queued transitions become available in creation order

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The platform-side approval path cannot complete — no Admin available, or the root unreachable for a critical-class decision
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The request remains visibly pending in the single approval queue; aging critical requests re-notify the root
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The change simply does not apply. There is no automatic approval and no configuration exists that could create one
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform continues on its last approved configuration; six ENFORCED invariants and the deterministic on-device layer untouched
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The decision is taken when an authorised approver returns; queue preserves creation order and each request's full age

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Authority population cannot satisfy a required handoff — no Supervisor on shift, or no Quality Manager reachable while a Severity 1 hold stands
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Escalation resolves to on-shift holders; where none exist, marked fallback delivery to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the Quality Manager role has no holder at all, a doubly-marked fallback to the Tenant Admin plus a tenant-configuration alarm (DEC-QMNONE-001)
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The Severity 1 hold remains in force on confirmed devices and propagating on others; no work resumes on held material
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Tenant Admin assigns a Quality Manager; the pending release request is delivered with full evidence and original creation timestamp preserved

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The floor handoff cannot complete because the device cannot reach the platform for an extended period
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The device continues on its pinned package, cached credentials within the offline trust window, and its locally-held queue of capture events
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Beyond the trust window, cached credentials and clearances are no longer trusted; the qualification gate blocks and the run parks
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A controlled stop; captures retained in the device's encrypted store which never touches the device gallery; Severity 1 holds remain in force
failures_fallbacks.recovery: At reconnection the device drains its queues and applies pending commands under the DEC-SYNC-001 three-phase order

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The Quality Manager decision cannot be obtained while material is held
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Escalation re-notifies on the Critical schedule (4 hours standard, 1 hour Regulated-Industry) and routes to every on-shift Quality Manager
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Marked fallback to the Quality Manager role irrespective of shift; where the role has no holder, DEC-QMNONE-001 applies
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The hold stands. Under no circumstance does a timer, agent, escalation tier, or record-finish window release a hold
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The decision is taken when an authorised Quality Manager acts; original creation timestamp preserved so the delay is measurable

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An incomplete audit stream — a surface's events fail to ingest into the tenant's single log
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Because change and audit commit in one transaction, an ingestion failure at the source cannot occur without the change also failing
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Downstream aggregation failure — the consolidated view must display an explicit completeness banner naming the affected window and surface
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The audit view enters a declared-incomplete state, remains readable, marked not suitable for compliance evidence until reconciled
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Aggregation replays from originating surfaces; immutable, idempotently keyed records cannot duplicate or overwrite

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A chain that cannot advance because the next stage has no eligible holder
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The item routes to the next configured tier and, for on-shift-resolved items, marked fallback to the Quality Manager role
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the constraint is structural (Reviewer must differ from Author), no fallback can satisfy it and the chain stops
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A controlled hold: submission stays submitted, Job stays pending_approval, watch item stays raised, brief stays unacknowledged and flagged
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The tenant adds an eligible holder; queued items become actionable in creation order with original timestamps preserved

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An activity whose Accountable role is vacant
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The platform refuses any change leaving zero Tenant Admins or zero approver-capable holders while a Job exists
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Vacancies the source does not guard — no Supervisor for an Area with scheduled runs, no authoring-grant holder — surface only at runtime
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The affected activity holds; runs already assigned continue on pinned content; unassigned runs are not created; submissions do not advance
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The Tenant Admin fills the vacancy; held items become actionable in creation order

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A chain that cannot complete because a stage has no eligible decider
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Escalation resolves to all on-shift holders; first acknowledgement claims; gate items re-route to the next person per Studio-authored policy
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the constraint is structural, no routing satisfies it and the chain stops
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A controlled hold in every case. Nothing anywhere approves itself
failures_fallbacks.recovery: An eligible decider acts; original timestamps and full age preserved so the delay is measurable rather than erased

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The escalation cannot reach an eligible person
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: All on-shift holders of the target role at the Location are notified; the first acknowledgement claims the item
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Empty roster: marked fallback to the Quality Manager role irrespective of shift; empty QM role raises a configuration alarm plus doubly-marked delivery to the Tenant Admin
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The item remains open and visible; deterministic controls remain in force; nothing executes and nothing expires; a Severity 1 hold stands
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The item is delivered and claimed as soon as an eligible holder appears on the roster; original creation timestamp preserved

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A handoff stuck in a non-terminal state because a dependent record never settles — a command that never reaches applied
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The handoff sits in Resolved with reconciliation outstanding; the surface says the decision is complete and the device has not confirmed
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the device never returns at all, reconciliation cannot complete (interacts with DEC-WIPE-001)
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Handoff remains Resolved with an open reconciliation item against the device; device last-known state displayed with its age
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On the device's return, pending commands apply in order and reconciliation completes

failures_fallbacks.trigger: No authorised approver is available
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Escalation under section 18.12, including the marked fallback delivery to the Quality Manager role irrespective of shift
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No eligible approver exists at all, through staffing or a structural segregation-of-duties constraint
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Controlled hold, then safe stop for new work of that class; everything in force stays in force and everything in flight finishes safely
failures_fallbacks.recovery: An eligible approver is added or becomes available; held items become actionable in creation order

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Recipient unavailable — the routed role has on-shift holders but none acknowledges within the timer
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-route to the next configured tier and re-notify; Critical at 4 hours standard, 1 hour Regulated-Industry
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No tier acknowledges
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Controlled hold — gate item stays visible and unexecuted; held lot stays held; parked run stays parked; Job stays pending_approval
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The first acknowledgement from any tier claims the item with its original creation timestamp preserved

failures_fallbacks.trigger: No eligible recipient — role resolution returns an empty on-shift roster
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Marked fallback delivery to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, with the original target's miss recorded
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The Quality Manager role has no holder at all — DEC-QMNONE-001; recommended tenant-configuration alarm plus doubly-marked delivery to the Tenant Admin
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The item stays open and visible; nothing is dropped; nothing is approved; the Severity 1 hold stands
failures_fallbacks.recovery: An eligible holder appears or is assigned; the item delivers with its original timestamp

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Recipient's role revoked between routing and delivery
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The delivery to the now-ineligible identity is suppressed, the item re-resolves against the current roster, suppression recorded as a distinct notification state
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Re-resolution returns an empty roster, which routes into FB-HO-F2
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The item remains open; no action by the ineligible identity is accepted; attempted actions refused and audited as a security event
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Delivery to a currently eligible holder; prior acknowledgement stands as historical fact and the claim is released with its cause recorded

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Recipient offline — a Frontline user whose device cannot reach the platform
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The item is queued as a command applying at the device's next sync, in order; human decisions route in parallel to a connected role
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The device does not return within the offline credential trust window; the qualification gate blocks and the run parks
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A controlled stop for that run; captures remain in the encrypted store; locally placed Severity 1 holds remain in force; nothing is discarded
failures_fallbacks.recovery: At reconnection the device drains its queues and applies pending commands in order (DEC-SYNC-001 three-phase order)

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Notification channel unavailable — in-app delivery, email delivery, or both fail
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The surviving channel carries the delivery; in-app cannot be muted, making it the more reliable of the two by design
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Both channels fail. There is no third channel — SMS, OS push, webhooks, external recipients and quiet hours are all outside V1
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The handoff remains in Created with delivery outstanding and remains visible in the Command Center feed and the Hub record
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Delivery retried under a bounded schedule (retry schedule TBD under DEC-HO-RETRY-001)

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Duplicate handoff — the same trigger produces two records, or two people raise the same request
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: De-duplication at routing; machine-triggered duplicates merge and increase evidence; human-raised duplicates merge with both requesters recorded
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: De-duplication misses because the second record differs materially — they are not duplicates and are linked as related items, both decided
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: At most one actionable item per object per decision class; any additional record is Superseded and reconciled, never deleted
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Not applicable — duplicates do not block progress; the mechanism prevents confusion rather than failure

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Out-of-order handoff — a clearance arriving after a suspension, or an older command after a newer one
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The command channel applies commands at the device in order; out-of-order server transitions are refused per the permitted-transition table
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Ordering cannot be determined because of device clock skew (tenant-set ~5 minutes, ceiling 60 minutes)
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The safety-favouring interpretation — the more restrictive of the two states — plus a sync conflict for human resolution; never last-write-wins for authorisation
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The Quality Manager resolves the conflict; the resolution is audited

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Stale handoff whose object has moved on — dispositioned, cancelled, superseded or finished
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The item renders Superseded with the object's current state shown, original evidence preserved, and superseding controls removed rather than disabled
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The object's current state cannot be determined because a dependent record has not settled; the item shows last known state with its age, explicitly labelled
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No action is taken on a superseded item and no surface offers one; a late-arriving Severity 1 on an already-released lot still places a fresh hold
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Not applicable — a superseded handoff is complete; its evidence remains attached to the object for the record's full term

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The Delivery Operations Hub web application is unreachable or its platform services return errors
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The browser session degrades to a clearly marked read-only view of the last successfully loaded data with a freshness marker; every write control is disabled rather than queued
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The session cannot even render cached content
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A full-screen service-unavailable page naming the tenant, the time of last successful contact and the support route, offering no mutating action
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Automatic on service restoration; reconciliation is the audit-log comparison in 19.2

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Hub write failure
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Referenced as governing write failure alongside FB-DOH-CORE-001; defined in 19.2
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: not restated in this chunk
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: not restated in this chunk
failures_fallbacks.recovery: not restated in this chunk

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A command that cannot be delivered
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Continued queuing with the enforcement state held authoritatively server-side and rendered honestly as undelivered
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Authorised human escalation to the Supervisor and Quality Manager on shift, who can take the physical action the command was meant to cause; then a controlled hold blocking new assignment to the affected device or worker
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The device continues under its last validly applied state until the offline credential-trust window expires the cached authority
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Delivery at the next sync; reconciliation replays the ordered command queue and records any command that expired undelivered as an operational exception, never as applied
